text:
Jen Park: Quick status — I ran a controlled decode sweep to isolate kernel selection vs batching heuristics vs KV behavior. Same prompt set (1000 short prompts), identical decode params (temp=0.2, max_tokens=128, stop=['\n']), same RNG seed. Focus: fused vs unfused matmul kernels, batch-threshold tuning, and 'persist' vs 'replay' KV modes.

Marco Liu: Nice. Which harness did you use — synthetic or replay?

Jen Park: Replay harness using production traces sampled to keep seq len distribution (p95 ~ 512). I also ran a synthetic run with uniform seq lengths for sanity. Command for the replay run:

```
./rtbench \ 
  --model lm-large \ 
  --kernel fused \ 
  --batch-threshold 16 \ 
  --kv-mode persist \ 
  --prompts data/replay/1000_sample.json \ 
  --seed 42 \ 
  --decode "temp=0.2,max_tokens=128,stop=[\\n]"
```

Rachel Gomez: Results? numbers pls (latency p50/p95, tokens/s, memory).

Jen Park: Short dump:
- fused + batch-thresh 16 + persist: p50=45ms, p95=210ms, tokens/s=18k, GPU mem peak=13.6GiB
- unfused + batch-thresh 16 + persist: p50=57ms, p95=280ms, tokens/s=14k, GPU mem peak=12.9GiB
- fused + batch-thresh 8 + persist: p50=52ms, p95=230ms, tokens/s=15.5k
- fused + batch-thresh 16 + replay: p50=48ms, p95=320ms, tokens/s=12.1k, KV miss rate=~22%

Marco Liu: Interesting: replay spikes p95 even with similar p50. That smells like KV miss-induced decoding stalls. Did you capture kernel-level timelines?

Jen Park: Yes — perf trace shows stalls during kv refill where decode kernels wait for KV load ops (CUDA memcpy + unpack). For replay case, we saw synchronous eviction path kicking in at~60% load.

Tomás Rivera: Could quantization change this? If quant kernels are smaller, maybe batch packing differs and causes different kernel selection (fused/unfused). Did you try quant variant?

Jen Park: I ran int8-quant variant once: it prefers a different GEMM kernel (small-block matmul) and overall p50 improved ~8% but token throughput dropped due to more kernel launches. Noted tradeoff in profiler (launch overhead > compute win for short seqs).

Rachel Gomez: Tokenizer note: when we use replay traces, tokenization alignment matters a lot for stop sequences. I saw a few generators returning extra tokens because of tokenizer differences between host tokenization used to build the trace and the runtime tokenizer. Any mismatch there will bias quality/latency comparisons.

Jen Park: Good call. I enforced the exact tokenizer binary and version in the harness and re-checked checksums of encoded prompts. That removed a handful of long-tail p95 anomalies. Added check: compare encoded lengths before run, fail if mismatch > 0.

Marco Liu: For regression triage: can you push the fused/unfused perf traces and a minimized repro for the KV miss case? I'll try toggling async prefetch for KV loads and a different eviction policy (LRU->CLOCK) to see impact.

Jen Park: Pushed to /srv/rtbench/results/2237774444/ (trace.tar.gz + run_args.json). Minimal repro: small harness that replays 50 traces that hit the eviction boundary.

perf-bot: load-test finished: 2237774444 — artifacts uploaded (trace.tar.gz, metrics.csv).

Tomás Rivera: Proposed next steps: 1) try async KV prefetch + batch coalescing, 2) run grid for batch-threshold in {8,12,16,24} x kernel={fused,unfused} x kv={persist,replay}, 3) run quant vs fp16 with same kernel selection hooks. I'll coordinate job in the grid queue.

Jen Park: Perfect. I'll add the tokenizer checksum gate to the harness and re-run the synthetic parity sweep to produce an apples-style one-to-one comparison (same prompts, stops, decode params). Will post a short writeup with the trace-driven evidence and suggested runtime knobs. :thumbsup:

Marco Liu: Thanks — that should help narrow the perf/regression surface.
